3. Pouches of Gutkha were seized by the Food Inspector.

The said samples were sent to the State and the State Analyst has (2 of 3) [CRLMP-3160/2019] submitted a report that samples were adulterated as it did not conform to the prevention of P.F.A. Rules 1958.
Thereafter, a complaint was filed.
Petitioners applied for sending the samples to Central Food Laboratory.

Application was allowed by the Court vide order dated 23.08.2012.
4.
It is contended by counsel for the petitioners that valuable rights have been given to the accused under Sub-Section (2) of Section 13 to get the report from the Central Food Laboratory.
In exercise of the said right, petitioners have applied the application and Court has allowed the application and has directed that the samples be sent to Central Food Laboratory for analysis.
5. Learned Public Prosecutor has opposed the misc. petition.
It is contended that the samples were found to be adulterated and in matters involving the adulteration, Court should not exercise the inherent powers.
6. I have considered the contentions.
7. The complaint in this case was filed on 26.05.2011.
Orders were passed by the Court under Sub-Section (2) of Section 13 of the P.F.A. Act in 2012.
From order dated 17.07.2018, it is revealed that the samples have not been produced before the Court till date and have not been sent to the Central Food Laboratory till date.
8. In view of the fact that shelf life of the product was only two months, the samples were drawn on 27.05.2010 by the Food Inspector, a period of nine years has lapsed.

Continuation of proceedings would tantamount of abuse of process of Court and would result in grave injustice to the petitioners as their valuable right for getting the samples analyzed by Central Food Laboratory has been infringed.
In view of the same, misc. petition is allowed.
Proceedings pending before the Court below in Criminal Case No.1835/2011 are quashed.
Stay application stands disposed.
